## QUESTION 3: Traffic dropped after a core update and no AI-answer visibility

**Short answer:** Diagnose first, then rebuild existing content. Don't mass-publish AI articles.

- **Source of the method:** Search Engine Land describes this process. It is a general method, not a recommendation of any one vendor.
- **Diagnose (days 1–30):**
  - Confirm the update dates on Google's Search Status Dashboard.
  - Compare traffic before and after in Search Console, segmented by page, query, device and country.
  - Check the search results for new AI Overviews or lost featured snippets.
  - Check whether the volatility is industry-wide (Semrush Sensor, Sistrix Visibility Index).
  - Treat small drops as noise. A major drop calls for a content-quality review.
- **Rebuild (days 31–90):**
  - Add original insight and fuller topic coverage.
  - Consolidate overlapping pages with 301 redirects.
  - Show authorship and cite sources.
  - Remove search-engine-first tactics.
- **Reassess (days 91–180+):** expect gradual gains, possibly across several core updates.
- **AI-generated content:** the guide cites no specific Google policy. It says automation without meaningful value is a search-engine-first signal to avoid, and that automated text should be enhanced rather than published as-is.

## QUESTION 4: Comparing scoring and AI-citation tools for a small marketing team

**Short answer:** Free tiers are rare and platform coverage varies widely. Search Console integration is rarely documented, and done-for-you help is mostly limited to onboarding. Most data below comes from SE Ranking's roundup (SE Ranking sells SE Visible), cross-checked against the HubSpot and Rubik Digital pages (Rubik Digital is an agency that sells AI search services). "Not stated" means the sources say nothing.

| Tool | Free tier / trial | Search Console integration | AI platforms tracked | Done-for-you support |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AthenaHQ | Free Essential tier (300 credits) | Yes (also GA4) | 5 on free, 11 on Starter ($295/month) | Not stated |
| AirOps | 14-day trial | Yes (per HubSpot) | ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, AI Mode | Not stated |
| Otterly AI | Free trial | Not stated | ChatGPT, Perplexity, AI Overviews, Copilot, plus add-ons | Not stated |
| Peec AI | Free trial | Not stated | Choose 3 on paid plans (Rubik Digital); more on Enterprise | Live onboarding and prioritized recommendations |
| Profound | 7-day trial, 50 daily prompts | Not stated (offers CDN integrations) | 3 on trial, up to 9 on Enterprise | Dedicated specialist on Enterprise |
| SE Visible | 10-day trial | Not stated | ChatGPT, Gemini, AI Mode, AI Overviews | Not stated |
| Ahrefs Brand Radar | 5 daily prompts with any paid Ahrefs plan | Not stated | AI Overviews, AI Mode, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Copilot | Not stated |
| Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit | No free trial | Not stated | ChatGPT, Gemini, AI Overviews, AI Mode | Not stated |
| Writesonic GEO | Not stated | Not stated | ChatGPT, AI Overviews, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity | Customer success and tutorials, not a managed service |

- **Best fit for a small team:** AthenaHQ is the only tool with both a free tier and documented Search Console integration.
- **Paid starting points:** Peec AI has the most documented onboarding support among paid options. Otterly has the lowest entry price ($29/month).
- **Done-for-you:** none of these tools offers true managed service at small-team pricing, based on the sources.
- **Content quality:** these are tracking tools. Only AirOps and Writesonic are described as helping with content work, and I did not verify this.
